name: inserting_is_not_mating
why: THE FIRST ASSEMBLY CASE OF THE PROJECT, and it proves the thing that the census of the APIs (note 80q) had already written and that nobody had ever measured: «AddComponent5 places without mating -- four free bodies that look like an assembly». Inserting almost always succeeds: the part appears, the tree fills up, the rebuild is clean. And the component is just lying there. An assembly of free parts opens, rotates, exports and gets assembled wrong, without any error saying so.
_how_it_was_written_before_and_why_it_wa: The first draft said: «the remaining degrees of freedom are the ONLY measure of this family that can fail in the right way -- six is the number expected on a component just inserted: three translations and three rotations». It was false in three points, and the case found out on the first run. (1) Six was not a possible return: GetRemainingDOFs returns a STATE of swRemainingDofs_e, not a count. (2) The measured value, 2, is swRemainingDofs_Unavailable. (3) The same 2 comes out on a FIXED component and on a free one, so that number does not tell apart the two things the case wanted to tell apart. It is kept written here because the mistake was not in the measurement: it was in having decided the expected number BEFORE measuring it, computing it from how one imagines an API works.
_what_it_measures_now: The two things that really work: IsFixed (it tells the first component, nailed down, from the others) and the count of GetMates. Not fixed and zero mates means RESTING, and that is known for certain. How free it is is not known, and the case demands that the bridge SAY so instead of making it up.

expect.why: the preparation inserted only one: «cover» has «to_insert: false» on purpose, otherwise I would measure the work of the preparation believing I am measuring the operation
AND THE CIRCLE CLOSES ON GA1: the state of the assembly now exists and counts the components. Up to 0.91.0 it answered «assembly document: the assistant does not modify it yet» and nothing else.

expect.tolerance_why: The position goes from metres to millimetres and is rounded to three decimals: 0.05 mm covers that rounding and the noise of the rebuild. It is very wide compared with what it has to discriminate -- if the indices of the matrix were different, the number coming out would not be 30.04: it would be 0, or a rotation element between -1 and 1. There is no need to tighten it: what is needed is that a mistake shows.
expect.why: THIS EXPECTATION PROVES THE FORMAT OF THE MATRIX. The indices 9, 10, 11 of ArrayData are the translation: Z confirms it, 30 asked and 30 read. If they were others a zero or a rotation element between -1 and 1 would come out.
expect._and_the_MINUS_TWO_is_the_discovery: The first run demanded [0, 0, 30] and read [0, -2, 30]. It is not a reading error: **AddComponent5(x,y,z) positions the CENTRE of the bounding box, not the origin.** The cover is extruded in one direction only -- as `extrude_rectangle` always does -- so its origin lies on a face and not at mid-thickness: asking for the centre at z=30, the origin ends up at -2 in Y, half of the 4 mm. Verified by PREDICTION, not by fitting: with a second part 10 thick asked at zero, -5 was predicted before launching the probe, and -5 came out. That is why the field is called `origin_mm` and no longer `position_mm`: calling it «position» invited comparing it with the point ASKED, and the two almost never coincide. Neither of the two numbers is wrong -- they are two different things, and nothing said so.

expect.why: zero mates on a non-fixed component: it is the count that says «resting», and it holds even without knowing what shape the thing GetMates returns has

ONE, NOT ZERO: **SOLIDWORKS fixes the first component inserted by itself** in an assembly. The «base» came from the preparation and is nailed down; the «cover», inserted by the operation, is not. The first draft of this case demanded 0 -- and the probe had already shown it (base-1 fixed=True, cover-1 fixed=False) before the case was written: the fact was there and had not been brought in.
expect._why_it_counts: It is exactly the distinction GA5 exists to make. A fixed component does not move because someone NAILED it down, not because it is mated: if the fixed ones entered the count of the constrained ones, every assembly would look assembled starting from the first part. Here the count excludes them, and that is why «assembly_constrained» stays false with one fixed and one resting.

expect.why: GA5: the summary. Two resting parts are not an assembled assembly, and the state must say so in one line without the reader having to add up the degrees by hand.
the sentence, not the number: whoever confirms reads this

ENTRY GA8, and it is a defense and not a curiosity. `GetTotalTransform(true)` includes the explode transformation: on an assembly shown exploded, `origin_mm` would be the position IN THE EXPLODED VIEW -- plausible and wrong by ten centimetres, with no error. This case reads `origin_mm` two expectations further up: **this `false` is what makes that reading reliable.** It is always written, even when false: a field that appears only when things went wrong teaches nobody to look for it.
IsFixed WORKS, and it is the useful half of the question «is it constrained?». The first component inserted is fixed, this one is not.
THE TRUE CONCLUSION: not fixed and without mates means resting there. HOW FREE it is is not known, and indeed it is not said.

THIS EXPECTATION GUARDS A MISTAKE THAT WAS REALLY MADE. The first run demanded «degrees_of_freedom_remaining equal to 6» and measured 2 -- and 2 was not a count: it was `swRemainingDofs_Unavailable`. The return of GetRemainingDOFs is a STATE, not a number, and on this assembly it says «unavailable» on EVERY component, fixed or free. Meanwhile the bridge was printing «still has 2 degrees of freedom out of 6»: an invented number, an invented unit, and identical for a part nailed down and one that wobbled. If one day this field stopped saying «unavailable», it would mean SOLIDWORKS has started to supply the information -- and then the count can be published. As long as it says this, it cannot.
expect._measured_as: probe DofProva2, four conditions: assembly just built, component selected, assembly saved to disk, and after a real coincident mate (AddMate5 with swAddMateError_NoError). Always «unavailable», always with all six statuses at swDofStatus_Unused.

expect.why: whoever reads «assembly_constrained: true» must know that it means «every component has at least one mate», NOT «it no longer moves». One coincident mate leaves three of the six directions free (measured, Z-C14), and this state does not see them. What is not known is said, not implied.
the warning travels with the answer, not only in the catalogue: whoever reads this answer may never have read the description of the operation
